findings.claim: The export-abi.ts CONTRACTS list and the abi-drift.test.ts CONTRACTS list are two independent hardcoded lists; a future contract addition/rename updating only one silently leaves an ABI unchecked by the guard.
findings.challenge: Alternative: developers will update both. Counter-check: both lists currently match (verified by reading both files), so the defect is latent; rejected the alternative on the df-cycle-12 history where a forgotten manual step caused exactly this drift.

findings.claim: mintTicket calls _safeMint (external buyer callback) before _splitRevenue; a malicious buyer might exploit the ordering.
findings.challenge: Traced reentry paths: mintTicket is nonReentrant, so the buyer onERC721Received callback can only reach views or revert on guarded functions; mint and split are atomic in one tx, so any revert unwinds both. Reversing the order has identical atomicity. No reachable exploit.

findings.claim: Owner can front-run setFilmPrice against a buyer mint transaction.
findings.challenge: Buyer tx reverts with IncorrectPayment (fail-closed); gas loss only, no fund movement; owner is the trusted platform by design and the function is documented future-mints-only. No fund risk.

findings.claim: useMovieTicket constructs a new viem publicClient on every render.
findings.challenge: Pre-existing pattern not introduced by df-cycle-13 (the change only swapped the fee constant read); trivial cost; out of this change-checkup scope.
